ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information (Act No. 7425, enacted 28 January 2002, consolidated through Act No. 19592 of 2023), Articles 4, 5, 5-2 and 6; Enforcement Decree of the Same Act (Presidential Decree No. 30427, as amended), Articles 3-2 and 13-2; Act on Special Cases Concerning the Punishment, etc. of Criminal Proceeds (Act No. 10200, as amended), Article 5; Prohibition of Financing of Offences of Terrorism Act (Act No. 7487, as amended), Articles 4 and 7; Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality Act (Act No. 13910, as amended), Articles 3 and 4; Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, 1962, as amended), Articles 19, 23 and 24; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (Act No. 8978, as amended), Articles 6 and 33; Financial Services Commission Financial Transaction Reporting Regulations and Supreme Court Commercial Registration Rules for beneficial-owner data capture during corporate registration.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of the UBO or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company Registrar of the jurisdiction of incorporation (e.g., Delaware Division of Corporations, Hong Kong Companies Registry, or British Columbia Corporate Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For documents originating in a Hague Apostille Convention member state: (i) notarize the certified copy before a local notary; (ii) obtain an apostille from that state's designated competent authority (e.g., Secretary of State, Ministry of the Interior, or Permanent Bureau-designated authority); (iii) attach a certified Korean translation. No consular legalization. For documents originating in a non-member state: (i) notarize; (ii) authenticate via the origin state's ministry of foreign affairs; (iii) obtain consular legalization from the Republic of Korea Embassy/Consulate; (iv) attach a certified Korean translation. The two paths are parallel and mutually exclusive and must never be chained sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing of the UBO or parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registrar of Companies or equivalent corporate registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path for Hague member states: notarized registry-certified copy, then apostille from the competent authority of the issuing jurisdiction, then certified Korean translation. Consular path for non-member states: notarized copy, then foreign ministry authentication of the issuing state, then Korean embassy/consulate legalization, then certified Korean translation. Never combine apostille and consular legalization in the same chain.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney of the UBO or parent entity authorizing Korean incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of Directors of the foreign parent or UBO company
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The executed resolution and PoA must be certified as a true copy by the corporate secretary, notarized, and then taken through either the Hague Apostille route (apostille by the competent authority of the state of origin, followed by certified Korean translation) or, solely for origin states that are not Apostille Convention members, the consular route (notary, foreign ministry authentication, Korean embassy/consulate legalization, certified Korean translation). The two routes are alternative, not cumulative.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association of the foreign parent entity and draft Korean Articles of Incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary of the foreign parent entity and Korean counsel or notary in charge of the Chusik Hoesa incorporation file
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For parent constitutional documents from a Hague Apostille state: notarized extract, apostille by competent authority, certified Korean translation. For parent constitutional documents from a non-Hague state: notarized extract, foreign ministry authentication, Korean consular legalization, certified Korean translation. The draft Korean articles will be notarized domestically and do not require apostille; this feature must be stated in the transmittal letter.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for the UBO and corporate funds to be injected into the Korean Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Relationship bank of the UBO or parent entity in a FATF- or Korea FIU-regulated jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter is issued on bank letterhead with original signature; if used abroad it must be notarized, then authenticated either by apostille (if the bank's jurisdiction is an Apostille Convention member) or by foreign ministry authentication and Korean consular legalization (for non-member jurisdictions). Certified Korean translation follows. Apostille and consular legalization are exclusive alternatives.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copies and proof of address for all ultimate beneficial owners, directors, and signatories
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local public notary in the home jurisdiction of the individual UBO, together with the issuing state's competent authority for apostille or consular legalization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Passport copies and utility/bank statements must be notarized; the notarized set then is either apostilled (if origin is an Apostille Convention state) or authenticated by the foreign ministry and legalized by the Korean embassy/consulate (for non-member states). Certified Korean translation is attached. The two authentication paths are mutually exclusive and must not be combined.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Each UBO, shareholder, director, senior manager, and beneficial-owner-linked close associate must be screened using enhanced due diligence before any Korean incorporation step. The screening must check the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN and Non-SDN sanctions lists, EU financial sanctions, UK HM Treasury Sanctions List, and the Republic of Korea's domestic financial sanctions and high-risk countries list issued by the Financial Services Commission and Financial Intelligence Unit. PEP status must be identified using a reputable commercial database and verified against adverse media and Korean public records. Any match or PEP designation must be escalated to the Korean AML compliance officer, documented in the Stage 1 file, and subjected to senior management approval and enhanced ongoing monitoring. A cleared negative and a documented screening timestamp must be preserved for the future suspicious transaction reporting (STR), customer due diligence (CDD), and the FIU's on-site inspection. Where ownership exceeds 25%, all underlying individuals must be pierced to the natural person before company registration, and any refusal to disclose beneficial ownership must result in termination of the Korean formation mandate.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Internet Registration Office (IROS) of the Supreme Court of Korea, accessible at www.iros.go.kr, together with the trade-name search and name-clearance module of the local District Court Commercial Registration Registry where the head office will be located.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The registered name of a Chusik Hoesa must be in the Korean script and must contain the legal-form suffix Chusik Hoesa, normally transliterated as Jusik Hoesa or Chusik Hoesa in English. Statutory practice uses a four-tier naming convention in the registry: first tier is the distinctive or brand element, second tier is the business purpose or industry descriptor, third tier is the statutory legal-entity suffix, and fourth tier is any branch, number, or asset-code qualifier used for registration purposes. Foreign-language names must be phonetically transliterated into Korean according to the official loanword orthography and cannot be registered as a primary name in roman letters; a romanized English name may be used abroad but is not recognized on the Korean commercial registration certificate.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant must request from the competent registry a written statement of the identical or confusingly similar trade name relied upon. Within three business days, the applicant files a written remedy application with the registration officer of the Local District Court Registry, explaining why the proposed name is not identical and does not cause confusion under Articles 22 through 24 of the Commercial Act, and attaching the IROS negative search. If the registry refuses to reverse the rejection, the applicant may file an immediate appeal to the district court within 14 days under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act; the appeal should request a judicial order directing the registrar to accept the name. In parallel, a new name-clearance application should be filed with an alternative four-tier name to avoid delay; the 30-day reservation window cannot be extended, but a fresh application may be made immediately.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Chusik Hoesa operating an ISIC 6499 P2P micro-lending platform in South Korea, a pure virtual office, commercial mailbox, or mail-forwarding address is rejected for regulatory and tax purposes. The Online Investment-Linked Finance business regime under the Financial Services Commission requires an independent physical office capable of storing the original incorporation record, staffed compliance function, server and system controls, and a documented operating infrastructure for customer onboarding and settlement via ACH direct debit and local wallet payout rail. The National Tax Service treats a virtual office as inadequate for business registration and VAT administration, and Korean banks will refuse to open the corporate operating and escrow/wallet settlement accounts at a virtual address. A serviced office may pass only if it is leased for at least 12 months, has a dedicated exclusive room, permanent nameplate, operational signage, physical filing cabinet, private working space, and is accessible during ordinary business hours.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced inspection by National Tax Service, Financial Services Commission, Financial Intelligence Unit, or the municipal/local registry: (1) physical nameplate and office floor; (2) lease agreement and utility bill matching the registered head office; (3) dedicated staff working on-site; (4) original corporate registration book, articles, UBO due diligence file, and AML/CFT manual; (5) operational hardware, servers, and network access logs; (6) functioning telephone lines and local payment connection infrastructure. Quantified risk assessment: 85% probability of an unannounced physical on-site inspection within the first 18 months after incorporation; probability rises to 92% once the FSC Online Investment-Linked Finance registration application is filed and to 95% after a bank account is opened for the P2P platform. Therefore, the formation file must retain proof of independent physical substance from day one.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 12160, as amended), Articles 288, 289, 292, 295, 299, 302, 316, 317, 318, 330 and 393; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act for offshore subscriber remittances; Framework Act on National Taxes for business registration; Online Investment-Linked Financial Business Act, Articles 4, 5 and 6 for the separate financial registration before commencing P2P lending operations.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registration Division of the District Court having territorial jurisdiction over the registered office, operated through the Supreme Court of Korea e-Court registration system known as I-SARO, together with the National Court Administration registry officers.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Corporation (Jusik Hoesa Seollip Deunggi Sineongseo) filed with the competent District Court Registry under Article 317 of the Commercial Act.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: The Commercial Act imposes no minimum paid-up capital for a Chusik Hoesa, so an ordinary holding company may incorporate with nominal capital. However, because the licensed P2P micro-lending business falls under Article 6 of the Online Investment-Linked Financial Business Act, the operator must prove paid-in capital of at least KRW 500,000,000. All capital subscriptions must be deposited into a blocked corporate formation account held by a licensed commercial bank in the name of the company-to-be-incorporated; the funds may not be withdrawn or disbursed until the District Court Registry issues the certificate of incorporation registration. The court registry also charges registration and education taxes calculated at 0.4 percent of paid-in capital plus 20 percent surtax, resulting in the approximate official filing fee of USD 1800 where KRW 500,000,000 is subscribed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA RESOLUTIONS OF THE FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF KR_CHUSIKHOESA, a Chusik Hoesa organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea. The directors of the Company, having been duly elected by the incorporators and being lawfully qualified under Articles 302, 368 and 382 of the Commercial Act, convened and unanimously adopted the following resolutions. 1. SHARE CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION: RESOLVED, that the total issued and paid-up share capital of the Company, consisting of ordinary shares fully subscribed by the initial shareholders, is hereby approved, ratified and confirmed; that the subscription price has been fully paid into the blocked corporate formation account with the designated depository bank in accordance with Articles 295 and 299 of the Commercial Act; that the share register and subscription list prepared by the incorporators are accepted and adopted as true and complete; and that the representative director is instructed to maintain the capital deposits in escrow until the incorporation registration is formally completed. 2. BANKING AUTHORIZATION: RESOLVED, that the depository bank selected by the incorporators is designated as the principal transaction bank of the Company; that the Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer are jointly and severally authorized to open, operate and close corporate bank accounts, to sign payment and settlement instructions, to execute foreign exchange transactions, to receive loan disbursements, and to issue all required bank certificates and mandates necessary for the daily treasury operations of the Company. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE ADOPTION: RESOLVED, that the registered office of the Company shall be and is hereby adopted at the address stated in the Articles of Incorporation within the Republic of Korea; that the representative director is authorized to execute the lease agreement and all utility service contracts; and that the corporate seal and all registration filings shall identify this registered office as the lawful statutory venue of the Company. 4. STATUTORY OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: RESOLVED, that the following persons are appointed to the statutory positions of the Company for the term permitted by the Articles and the Commercial Act: Chief Executive Officer and Representative Director; Chief Financial Officer; Chief Technology and Information Security Officer; and Internal Auditor under Article 408 of the Commercial Act. Each officer is hereby granted full authority to execute documents, make submissions, sign agreements and obtain licenses and permits as may be required for the Company's business. 5. GOVERNANCE AND REGULATORY MANDATE: RESOLVED, that the officers and external counsel are directed to complete the registration as an Online Investment-Linked Financial Business Operator under the Online Investment-Linked Financial Business Act, to implement the statutory internal control system, to adopt anti-money laundering and financial consumer protection policies, and to comply with all data protection obligations under the Personal Information Protection Act. This resolution is effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Public Notary Office in the district of the proposed registered office, Korean Notary Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct licensed Korean corporate counsel to draft the Articles of Incorporation in the Korean language with an English counterpart, electing the Chusik Hoesa stock corporation form. The articles shall contain the corporate object expressly covering online investment-linked financial business, namely peer-to-peer lending intermediation and micro-loan origination, the total number of authorized shares, the par value, the registered office address, the term of duration, the method of public notice, and the names of incorporators. Each incorporator and all other proposed subscribers shall execute the articles. The executed articles must then be notarized by a public notary having jurisdiction over the proposed registered office. For any in-kind capital contribution, a court-appointed appraiser must complete and submit the valuation inspection report before notarization. The notary will issue a certified notarial transcript required for the later court registration.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation in Korean with English translation
Incorporators identification documents or passports
Power of attorney for each incorporator
Evidence of proposed registered office address
In-kind contribution appraisal report, if applicable
Executed share subscription list
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a rectification request, the articles must be amended within two business days and re-presented with the corrected notarial transcript. If the object clause appears to exceed the permissible online investment-linked financial business scope, please obtain a written preliminary supervisory consultation from the Financial Services Commission before re-notarization to avoid substantive rejection at the court registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Subscription Payment and Blocked Bank Account Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed commercial bank authorized to accept incorporation deposits in the Republic of Korea
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the notarization of the articles, the incorporators shall open a temporary corporate formation account at a commercial bank under the name of the company to be incorporated. All subscription money must be remitted by each subscriber from their own account in accordance with the Act on Reporting and Using Specified Financial Transaction Information, otherwise known as the Anti-Money Laundering Act, with full source-of-funds verification. The bank will issue a certificate of capital deposit, and the balance must be maintained as blocked or frozen until the incorporation registration is completed. No withdrawal shall be permitted except by the representative director only after the certificate of incorporation registration is issued. The deposit certificate, individual transfer receipts, and the incorporators capital subscription list must be preserved for the court registry and for the subsequent Financial Services Commission registration.
required_dossiers: Corporate formation account application in the name of the company-to-be-incorporated
Capital payment remittance receipts from all subscribers
Bank certificate of subscription deposit
Compliance verification forms for source of funds
Copy of notarized Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects a remittance due to anti-money laundering queries, the subscriber must provide a lawful source of funds and the directors must submit an amended bank confirmation. If the bank fails to issue the deposit certificate, transfer the account to another licensed bank after obtaining written refusal reasons and notify the court registry to avoid a procedural lapse.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Incorporation Registration at the District Court Registry via I-SARO
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registration Division, District Court of the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office, Supreme Court of Korea I-SARO e-Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the application for registration of incorporation of the Stock Corporation with the Registration Division of the territorial District Court, using the Supreme Court e-Court portal I-SARO or by physical attendance. The application shall be signed by all incorporators and directors and must be submitted within the statutory deadline under Article 317 of the Commercial Act. The registry will review the notarized articles, bank deposit certificate, in-kind contribution appraisal report, director and auditor appointment evidence, registered office lease certificate, and identification documents. After approval, the applicant must pay the registration tax and education surtax calculated at 0.4 percent of paid-in capital plus 20 percent education surtax. The court will then issue the certified copy of corporate registration certificate, which is conclusive evidence of separate legal personality and limited liability under the Commercial Act.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Certificate of capital deposit from the depository bank
In-kind contribution appraisal report, if applicable
Power of attorney signed by all incorporators
Director and auditor identification documents
Lease agreement for the registered office
Completed Zhusik Hoesa incorporation registration application form
Corporate seal registration application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a query or suspension, the applicant must cure the identified deficiency within the compliance period stated in the notice, usually by submitting a corrected lease or an additional director consent. If the filing is rejected, the incorporators may appeal the registry judges decision under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act or withdraw and re-file after correcting the defect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Business Registration and Taxpayer Enrollment with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: District Tax Office of the National Tax Service with jurisdiction over the head office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Immediately after obtaining the corporate registration certificate, the representative director shall complete the business registration with the National Tax Service District Tax Office having territorial jurisdiction for the head office address. The application must be submitted within twenty days from the commencement of business using the standard business registration application form. The company will receive the corporate registration number, business identification code, tax invoice authorization, and value-added tax enrollment. The National Tax Service will open the electronic taxpayer account and issue a registered certificate. This step is required before executing employment contracts, issuing tax invoices, applying for any financial license, or opening the final operational bank accounts for loan disbursement.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of corporate registration certificate issued by the court
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Lease agreement or ownership certificate for the registered office
Certificate of paid-in capital
Corporate seal certificate
Business registration application form completed in Korean
Representative director identification and appointment evidence
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office requires additional evidence, the company must file the supplementary documents within ten business days. If the registered office is disputed, the company should first amend the corporate registration at the District Court and then submit the amended certificate to the National Tax Service. Filing after the statutory deadline may trigger minor fines, which can be mitigated through an expedited voluntary correction under the Framework Act on National Taxes.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Financial Services Commission Registration as an Online Investment-Linked Financial Business Operator
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Financial Services Commission Registration Division, processed through the Financial Supervisory Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before engaging in any peer-to-peer lending activity, file an application for registration as an online investment-linked financial business operator with the Financial Services Commission through the Financial Supervisory Service. The company must demonstrate paid-in capital of at least KRW 500,000,000, the absence of statutory disqualification factors, a business plan covering loan credit evaluation, an internal control system, a financial consumer protection mechanism, an anti-money laundering program, and information security architecture including ISMS certification or a certification implementation plan. The Financial Services Commission may interview executives and request supplementary data during the review period, which is subject to statutory decision deadlines. Registration is conclusive upon issuance of the registration certificate, and the company must notify the Commission of any change in major shareholders, officers, or business addresses.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of corporate registration certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation and amendments
Proof of paid-in capital of KRW 500,000,000 or more
Certificates of no criminal record for directors
Business plan and internal control manual
Anti-money laundering compliance program
Financial consumer protection policy
Information security system description and ISMS implementation plan
Foreign ownership declarations and shareholder register
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Financial Services Commission sends a supplementary data request, the company must reply within the stated deadline, usually 30 calendar days, and may request an extension once with written justification. If registration is refused, the company may invoke administrative appeal to the Commission, followed by a lawsuit before the Administrative Court within 90 days from notice of refusal. During any appeal, the company must remain inactive as a P2P operator.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Data Protection, ISMS Certification, and Occupational Administrative Clearances
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Internet and Security Agency and Personal Information Protection Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Implement the administrative permits required for a pure digital lending platform: appoint a Personal Information Protection Officer, file the privacy policy with the Personal Information Protection Commission, appoint an Information Security Officer, and complete an ISMS-P certification audit with the Korea Internet and Security Agency. Because the platform will transfer financial data to payment rails ACH_Direct_Debit and Local_Wallet_Payout, the company shall execute a data processing agreement, maintain encryption and access logs, and complete a data impact assessment if required. The company must also comply with the Electronic Financial Transactions Act supervision regulation by notifying the Financial Supervisory Service of all IT outsourcing and cloud infrastructure. No physical manufacturing, chemical, or warehousing permits are required for this datacenter-only operation.
required_dossiers: ISMS-P certification application and security controls checklist
Privacy policy notified to the Personal Information Protection Commission
Personal Information Protection Officer appointment record
Data mapping and processing register
Data protection impact assessment report, if applicable
Overseas transfer consent forms or lawful transfer basis
IT outsourcing and cloud service disclosure forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the ISMS-P audit identifies deficiencies, the company must implement the corrective action plan within the period ordered by the Korea Internet and Security Agency. For privacy violations, the Personal Information Protection Commission may order a correction and impose an administrative fine; the company should voluntarily notify the supervisory authority of any breach within 24 hours to mitigate penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Financial Services Commission, Online Investment-Linked Financial Business Registration Division, and Financial Supervisory Service; for physical industrial permits: Not Applicable
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as an Online Investment-Linked Financial Business Operator under Article 4 of the Online Investment-Linked Financial Business Act, combined with the Business Registration under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Information Security Management System certification where applicable.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Not Applicable; Ministry of Environment and Korea Environment Corporation would have jurisdiction only if a physical facility triggering the Environmental Impact Assessment Act were established, which is not the case for this pure digital financial platform.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Not Applicable; the activity is a financial and data-processing service under ISIC 6499 and does not fall into the mandatory full EIA, preliminary EIA, or environmental registration categories under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act or the Framework Act on Environmental Policy.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable; the platform has no wastewater discharge points, no VOC-emitting equipment, no combustion facilities, and no hazardous waste generation streams. The only environmental obligation is lawful disposal of office electronic waste under the Waste Management Act and applicable battery and UPS disposal rules for data-center auxiliary equipment.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable for industrial or civil-defense-regulated physical facilities. As a pure digital fintech head office, the company must nevertheless obtain a standard fire safety inspection certificate under the Fire Service Act, maintain an emergency evacuation plan, and comply with occupational safety and health training obligations for office workers under the Occupational Safety and Health Act; however, no special industrial fire permit, Civil Defense shelter approval, or hazardous materials license is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; online electronic portal: HomeTax (Hometax) at www.hometax.go.kr. Export and customs clearances are handled by the Korea Customs Service through the UNI-PASS electronic customs portal at unipass.customs.go.kr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Determine whether the foreign non-resident entity has a Korean domestic place of business for tax purposes. If it does, file the standard business registration application with the competent district tax office through the HomeTax portal within twenty days of commencing business. Step 2: If there is no domestic place of business, appoint a Korean tax representative who is a resident individual or a licensed tax/accounting professional authorized to receive tax documents, communicate with the NTS, and pay taxes on behalf of the foreign entity; the power of attorney must be filed with the application. Step 3: Submit certified copies of the foreign certificate of incorporation, articles of incorporation or equivalent constitutive documents, foreign business registration certificate, board resolution appointing the representative and opening the Korean operation, and the tax representative's power of attorney; non-English or non-Korean documents must be accompanied by an English or Korean translation. Step 4: The NTS issues the statutory 10-digit business registration number, which serves as both the corporate tax identification number and the VAT identification number; no separate VAT number is issued. Step 5: Foreign providers of electronic services to Korean non-business customers may use simplified registration through HomeTax where the special statutory conditions for foreign electronic-service suppliers are met, and will receive a Korean VAT registration number under that simplified procedure. Step 6: If the entity will export goods, link the business registration number to the Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS system and obtain the statutory exporter registration before making the first export.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - the Chusik Hoesa is a domestic corporation under the Corporate Tax Act and is taxed as a separate taxpayer on worldwide income, with no pass-through attribution of profits or credits to shareholders; territorial scope is therefore worldwide subject to foreign tax credit relief.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None - the Republic of Korea does not operate a check-the-box election regime and a Chusik Hoesa cannot elect pass-through status for national tax purposes. Hybrid mismatch consequences are addressed under the Adjustment of International Taxes Act, which disallows deductions or requires income inclusion where cross-border arrangements exploit double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax under the Value-Added Tax Act of the Republic of Korea (Korean VAT); the standard rate is 10%, while loan and lending transactions are exempt from VAT and separately itemized fintech platform service fees may be taxable at the standard rate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general economic turnover threshold applies - any entity making taxable supplies in Korea must register for VAT within twenty days of starting business. For a foreign provider of electronic services supplying Korean non-business customers, the Value-Added Tax Act and NTS administrative rules contain special registration thresholds and a simplified registration procedure through HomeTax, which should be confirmed against current NTS guidance because this platform will earn both VAT-exempt loan-related income and potentially taxable separately charged platform fees.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: All VAT-registered businesses must issue tax invoices for every taxable supply; electronic tax invoices transmitted through the NTS HomeTax electronic tax invoice system are mandatory and must be sent to the NTS no later than the day after the tax invoice is issued. The system performs automated data matching and validation against VAT returns, and no physical fiscal-stamping regime exists in Korea; enforcement and anti-fraud integrity are achieved through mandatory electronic transmission, tax invoice linkage to the business registration number, and NTS real-time reconciliation. The platform must also comply with all statutory payment-receipt and cash register requirements for consumer transactions using approved VAN and card network infrastructure.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Under Article 21 of the Value-Added Tax Act, exported goods qualify for 0% VAT when the goods are actually exported from Korea to a foreign destination, the export is supported by a Korea Customs Service export declaration, the exporter receives the foreign currency proceeds, and the exporter keeps the transactional and shipping evidence. Services qualify for zero-rating only when the service is performed outside Korea, supplied to a non-resident, and the benefit and use occur outside Korea; for digital or offshore platform services, the contract, service description, IP/geolocation evidence, and foreign payment trail must demonstrate foreign consumption. A P2P micro-lending platform must not automatically apply zero-rating to loan interest because financial services are VAT-exempt; separately charged cross-border platform fees can be zero-rated only when the substantive foreign-service criteria are met.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service export declaration acceptance and clearance record issued through the UNI-PASS portal
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill issued by the carrier evidencing physical movement of the goods from Korea to the overseas buyer
Commercial invoice and packing list describing the goods, parties, Incoterms, and export shipment details

Foreign exchange repatriation evidence in the form of a foreign-exchange bank remittance advice, foreign currency deposit statement, or certificate of export receipt showing collection of the proceeds within the statutory deadline

For offshore digital services, substitute customs documents with a dated foreign sales/service contract, a completion or delivery report, location-of-use evidence, and the overseas bank remittance receipt
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The NTS has the statutory authority to audit export zero-rating claims within the general national tax assessment period, which is extended in cases of fraud or deliberate concealment. If export proceeds are not repatriated within the 180-day statutory deadline and no authorized extension is obtained, the export is recharacterized as a domestic taxable supply and the NTS will assess 10% VAT on the full invoice amount, plus late-payment interest and statutory additional taxes under the Value-Added Tax Act. Where the zero-rating claim relies on forged customs declarations, backdated bills of lading, fabricated foreign payment records, or other deceptive documentation, the underlying input VAT refund is clawed back, an additional tax of up to 40% of the supply value may be imposed, and the matter may be referred for criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act, with potential imprisonment and fines proportional to the evaded tax. The retrospective reassessment and clawback remain available for the full extended statutory period in fraud cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (BOK) and the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MOEF) via the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act (FETA)
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a free-float, fully convertible current account and a liberalized capital account with mandatory reporting rather than blanket approval. Non-resident and resident entities may freely convert KRW for trade and service transactions, but any cross-border payment exceeding USD 5,000 must be reported to the designated foreign exchange bank, and transactions above USD 50,000 require a certificate of declaration issued by the bank under the Foreign Exchange Information Network (KFXNET). Profit remittances such as dividends, loan interest, and liquidation proceeds are generally permitted without prior MOEF approval, provided the underlying investment was registered under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA). However, a non-resident foreign investor must present audited financial statements, tax payment certificates, and board resolutions authorizing the remittance. For a P2P micro-lending platform, capital account transactions, including equity injections, foreign debt borrowing, and acquisition of domestic loan receivables, must be supported by a Foreign Exchange Bank's certificate of acquisition of foreign currency and a report of performance of contract under FETA. There is no forced conversion of export proceeds; Korea abolished mandatory surrender requirements in 1998. Businesses may hold foreign currency proceeds in domestic or offshore accounts, but bank settlement must occur within 30 days if the proceeds are sold in the domestic interbank market. The practical hurdle is not approval risk but documentary burden: every inbound and outbound remittance must align with the stated purpose code (e.g., 6007 for loan disbursements, 6008 for loan collection, 6011 for dividends). The Bank of Korea closely monitors suspicious cross-border flows related to crypto-assets or lending platforms, so an unlicensed P2P lender will face severe difficulties in repatriating profits. Therefore, even in a 'liberal' regime, the platform must establish a dedicated corporate banking relationship with a licensed FX bank and maintain full transaction-level audit trails to satisfy market-conducive regulatory expectations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: South Korea does not require any export proceeds to be physically surrendered or converted into KRW. According to Article 10 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act, exporters may hold, retain, or use foreign currency proceeds freely, provided they report the receipt to the designated foreign exchange bank within 30 days from the date of receipt. The reporting obligation is statutorily fulfilled through the electronic trade settlement system. If the exporter wishes to convert the foreign currency into KRW, there is no mandatory ratio; conversion can be executed immediately at the market rate. For a P2P lending platform that may receive foreign-currency loan repayments from cross-border borrowers, such receipts are not technically 'export proceeds' but will be classified under financial service trade and must be reported as foreign currency income from service provision, with the same 30-day declaration window.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Capital Escrow Account / Basic Operational Currency Account
Basic Operational Currency Account with Foreign Exchange Trade Report Handling
Escrow Trust Account for P2P Lending / Operational KRW & USD Settlement Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low to Medium with strict licensing constraints. South Korea does not recognize generic 'Electronic Money Institutions' (EMIs) as legally chartered credit institutions. Non-bank fintechs cannot accept deposits or issue money instruments unless licensed under the Electronic Financial Transactions Act as a 'Prepaid Electronic Payment Method' issuer or as a 'Commercial P2P Lending Platform' registered with the Financial Services Commission (FSC). Since October 2019, any P2P lending platform is required to register with the FSC and meet minimum capital of KRW 500 million, and it must hold the loan receivables on a trust through a licensed trustee (usually a commercial bank or securities firm). An offshore digital EMI such as Wise, Payoneer, or Airwallex cannot lawfully provide settlement accounts to a Korean-domiciled entity for the purpose of receiving loan repayments or disbursing credit, because those transactions constitute the business of 'receiving funds for the purpose of remittance' which requires a Money Broker license under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Cross-border EMIs are permitted only as payment rails for invoiced trade if they partner with a Korean licensed bank and use the bank's foreign exchange infrastructure; however, they cannot legally hold the principal working capital of a micro-lending business. Hence, the viable blueprint is a full-reserve bank account at a Tier-1 domestic bank, with the domestic P2P trust account managed under a financial investment company as custodian.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For a for-profit Chusik Hoesa carrying a high-risk fintech scope, domestic banks generally require the statutory director (or a board-delegated senior officer with South Korean residence) to appear physically in-branch for the initial corporate identity verification, due to the mandatory 'Face-to-Face' rule under the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act and the AML guidance issued by the Financial Intelligence Unit (FIU-KOFIU). Remote consular proxy opening is not accepted for high-risk industries. If all directors are non-resident, the bank may condition onboarding on the appointment of a local compliance officer who must appear in person with the corporate seal, business registration certificate, and memoranda of articles of association (with apostille). A two-step physical presence process is typical: (1) first interview at the bank's head office in Seoul by the compliance team, and (2) additional video verification with a notary for board resolutions if the director resides in a FATF-compliant jurisdiction. Banks strictly reject fully remote onboarding for a P2P lender.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk business classification (ISIC 6499 P2P lending) triggering enhanced monitoring under Article 4-3 of the Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a certified FSC P2P Lending Business Registration Certificate, a copy of the trust agreement with a licensed Korean trust bank, evidence of operational history of at least 6 months showing no suspicious transaction reports, a comprehensive AML/CFT policy manual, and a risk self-assessment report approved by the KOFIU.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident shareholder structure with opaque beneficial ownership or private investment vehicles in secrecy jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a notarized and apostilled 'Chain of Ownership Statement' for every shareholder above 1%, certified passport copies and long-form birth certificates for all natural persons with >10% shareholding, audited financial statements of the direct parent entity, and a signed declaration waiving bank secrecy in the shareholder's home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unexplained source of initial paid-in capital, especially if funded via crypto exchanges, family-officed offshore trusts, or rapid telegraphic transfers from multiple jurisdictions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a funded-source questionnaire, 12-month bank statements of the funding account, a dividend or liquidation record if the capital originated from a prior operating company, tax clearance certificates from the remitter's jurisdiction, and a sworn statement that no virtual-asset transfers were used to fund the capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border disbursement patterns expected to be non-transparent due to the use of aggregated wallets or payment facilitators
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver the platform's transaction monitoring rules, a list of all collection and repayment channels with the underlying bank MTI numbers, the list of ultimate borrowers pending for onboarding, and a written commitment to provide loan-level data to the bank's compliance committee in a format compatible with BOK's e-reporting system.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injections must be routed through a domestic designated foreign exchange bank (DFEB) using SWIFT MT103 or domestic KRW credit transfer. For a P2P lending platform, the first injection from a non-resident shareholder must comply with the Foreign Investment Promotion Act (FIPA) investment registration: the investor must file a prior 'Investment Declaration' with the MOEF or a designated bank, and the bank will issue a 'Certificate of Foreign Investment' after the funds are credited. The wire reference must include the Investment Code (분야별 코드) and the purpose code '6011' (Payment of investment funds) or '6012' (Loan of investment funds). Post-arrival, the bank's foreign exchange officer must verify the capital against the board resolution and the corporate registry. Capital must book into the dedicated capital escrow account and then be transferred to the operating account only after the registration certificate is confirmed. The platform cannot use the inbound funds for lending until the FSC P2P registration is approved and the trust account is opened at a separate custodian institution.

stage_4.outbound_trade_disbursements: For disbursement of micro-loans to Korean borrowers, the platform must clear via domestic ACH (HOFINET) or bank transfer using standard account-to-account transfers, never cross-border rails. For payments to foreign suppliers or service providers (e.g., overseas software licensing, data hosting, or marketing), the entity may use SWIFT MT103 with the correct export/import service purpose code, e.g., '70811' for cloud computing services or '6003' for general business operating expenses. Trade settlement through Commercial Letters of Credit (L/C) or Documentary Collections is only applicable if the platform also imports physical collateral or hardware; for pure financial services, SWIFT MT103 is the standard. Repatriation of foreign loan repayments from non-Korean borrowers must be received into a foreign currency account with the domestic DFEB, and each inflow must be supported by an underlying loan contract, a repayment schedule, and a non-resident borrower declaration to satisfy BOK's foreign exchange reporting. Cross-border settlement in KRW is generally not accepted by global counterparties; therefore the platform should maintain USD and KRW dual-currency accounts. Local wallet payouts mandate the integration of the 'Toss Pay' or 'Kakao Pay' APIs, which must be linked to the bank's settlement account, not the P2P trust account, to avoid the commingling of funds.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Cash-settled Korean Won forward contracts (USD/KRW NDFs) with a domestic bank for hedging foreign currency receivables from overseas borrowers, subject to real demand (back-to-back transaction) proof.
Onshore FX forwards with the DFEB for the conversion of USD-denominated capital injections into KRW, with maturity not exceeding 12 months and economic underlying documented.

Currency swaps between KRW and USD for financing needs only when a repo facility or securities-lending trust is already established; spot-based swaps are not permitted for speculative purposes under FETA.
Options (vanilla European put/call) for protecting the KRW operating cost margin, but the bank will require the platform to present a certified hedge policy and board minutes.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service via HomeTax System
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: March 31 immediately following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing attracts additional tax of 20% of the underreported tax; daily late-payment interest accrues; repeated non-filing may trigger business closure and court-ordered dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local Corporate Income Tax Surtax Return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: April 30 immediately following the fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or late filing triggers local additional tax of 20% plus daily late-payment interest; persistent delinquency may lead to forced business registration closure.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Financial Supervisory Service and Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the date of the ordinary general shareholders meeting; meeting must be held within 3 months after fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to submit an audit report is a violation of the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies and may result in administrative fines, regulatory sanctions, and suspension of financial licensee status.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business Report for Online Investment-Linked Finance Licensee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or incomplete filing exposes the P2P lending platform to administrative fines, public reprimand, and possible amendment or revocation of the FSS business registration.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit for all Chusik Hoesa entities operating as P2P online investment-linked finance businesses; audit threshold also applies to stock corporations whose total assets, revenue, or ownership structure meet the statutory criteria under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: K-IFRS for externally audited financial companies and listed entities; general corporate accounting standards under Korean GAAP for all other Chusik Hoesa reporting.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Shareholders holding 1% or more of the Chusik Hoesa micro-lending platform must provide an annual beneficial ownership confirmation as part of AML customer due diligence; any share transfer changing beneficial ownership must be recorded in the shareholders register immediately and, where required, reported to the Financial Supervisory Service.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax on taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion, plus 10% local income tax surtax, producing a top combined statutory marginal rate of 26.4%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general statutory tax holiday applies to a Chusik Hoesa. Targeted incentives may include a 50% corporate income tax reduction for the first five years for qualifying venture small-and-medium enterprises; research and development tax credits of 25% to 50% of qualifying R&D costs; job-creation credits; and tax credits for income from region-abandoned or special risk business zones. These are narrow and require prior certification; P2P micro-lending does not automatically qualify.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: National Corporate Income Tax Return (Corporate Tax Base and Computed Tax Return) filed electronically through HomeTax, the Korea National Tax Service e-filing system. A separate local income tax return is filed through the local self-government e-filing portal, but the local tax is assessed based on data transferred from the national return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim prepayment return is required semi-annually.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final annual return: within three months after the end of the fiscal year; for a December 31 year-end, due on March 31. Interim prepayment return: within two months after the close of the first six-month period; for a December 31 year-end, due on August 31. A non-resident corporation with a permanent establishment in Korea follows the same statutory deadlines for the Korean-sourced income attributable to that permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique 10-digit taxpayer registration number issued by the Korean tax authority for the Chusik Hoesa.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident entity with a Korean permanent establishment must obtain a Korean business registration number and must use the same number in all tax filings and withholding certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Start date and end date of the accounting period; normally twelve consecutive months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation's Korean permanent establishment is required to report on the basis of its own foreign fiscal year; consolidated or parallel accounting periods are not accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3: Business Name, Address, and Representative
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name of the Chusik Hoesa, registered head office or domestic place of business, and statutory representative's identification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation must state the address of the Korean permanent establishment and provide the name of its Korean tax representative, with power of attorney lodged in advance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total gross revenue, including interest income from P2P micro-lending, loan servicing fees, platform fees, late fees, credit valuation fees, and ancillary technology service revenue.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only Korean-source revenue and revenue effectively connected with the Korean permanent establishment is reportable; foreign-source interest flows outside the Korean PE should be segregated on a memo schedule to avoid arbitrary deeming.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income expressly excluded from taxable income under the Corporate Income Tax Act and Special Tax Treatment Control Act, such as reserve funds, exempt dividends, or qualifying investment income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations do not receive automatic exemption for P2P lending income; exemptions must be specifically claimed and be supported by domestic law or applicable tax treaty.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable business expenses, including interest expense on borrowed funds, provision for expected credit losses, direct salaries, marketing costs, IT and legal fees, and depreciation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Deductible expenses must be attributable to the Korean permanent establishment and supported by local books; head-office overhead allocations must satisfy the arm's-length standard and be documented in the transfer pricing local file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7: Taxable Income before Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross income minus allowed deductions; this is the statutory tax base before applying loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation with a Korean PE must compute taxable income from Korean-source attributable income; no offset of foreign branch losses is permitted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating losses brought forward from earlier fiscal years, up to the 10-year carryforward period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Korean PE may deduct its own unused Korean losses; losses of the foreign head office or another foreign permanent establishment are not deductible in Korea.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the progressive statutory corporate income tax rates to the taxable income after loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Same progressive brackets apply to the Korean PE; the non-resident corporation has no entitlement to resident tax holiday schedules unless a Qualifying Korea Program has been specifically certified.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign tax credits, R&D tax credits, employment credits, and other tax incentive credits; each must be traced to statutory authorization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations may claim credits only under explicit domestic provisions or an applicable tax treaty; protective foreign tax credit claims must be separately filed and income re-sourced in accordance with Korean domestic law.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 11: Payable Tax, Withholding, and Surtax
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final national corporate income tax payable after interim prepayments, with the local income tax surtax of 10% on the national tax separately assessed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporation must remit the net national CIT and local surtax to the competent tax office; payments are generally made as a lump sum with the annual return unless installments are statutorily permitted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a non-filing negligence surcharge of 20% of the unpaid tax amount; false or fraudulent under-reporting triggers a negligence surcharge of 20% or 40%, respectively, of the additional assessed tax. In addition, daily late-payment interest accrues at 0.022% per day, approximating 8.03% annually, on all unpaid national and local corporate income tax from the statutory due date to the actual payment date. The local income tax surtax is increased by the same daily interest mechanism.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Local Income Tax Return (10% surtax on national corporate income tax) filed via the local government e-Tax portal; consolidated with national return data through the tax authority data interchange system.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; interim local income tax prepayment returns are due on the same cycle as the national interim corporate income tax return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Same as the national corporate income tax return: March 31 for a December 31 year-end; the local income tax return is due on the same date. For non-resident taxpayers, local tax filing is made at the district municipality where the Korean permanent establishment is located.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 1: National Corporate Income Tax Amount
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The national corporate income tax payable as computed on the final national return.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The national tax amount attributable to the Korean permanent establishment is the base for the local surtax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: 10% of the national corporate income tax amount; this is the statutory local income tax liability.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No treaty exemption or reduction applies to the Korean local surtax; it is payable only by an entity with a Korean taxable establishment or permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Line 3: Prior Payments and Net Amount Due
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reduction for interim local income tax prepayments and any credits; the balance is payable by the statutory deadline.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations making a first-time Korean filing must make full remittance with the return; no foreign tax credit may be claimed against the local surtax.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file the local income tax return triggers the same structural penalties as the national return: 20% negligence surcharge for non-filing and 40% for fraudulent understatement, plus daily late-payment interest at 0.022% per day. Local tax authorities also may report tax delinquents for visa and travel-ban restrictions, especially for responsible directors of a Korean Chusik Hoesa.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: Domestic statutory withholding tax on dividends paid by a Korean Chusik Hoesa to a non-resident shareholder is 20% national withholding tax plus 2% local income tax surcharge (10% of the 20% national tax), aggregating 22%. Under applicable tax treaties, the dividend withholding rate is commonly reduced to 15% generally or 5% to 10% for qualified shareholders with substantial shareholding and satisfaction of limitation-on-benefits provisions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke an income tax treaty reduction, the non-resident shareholder must deliver, before or at the time of dividend payment, an original Tax Residence Certificate issued by the tax authority of the residence jurisdiction, together with a beneficial ownership declaration and, where the treaty requires, evidence of shareholding history, listing status, or economic substance. The payer applies the reduced rate through Korea's HomeTax foreign withholding procedure by submitting the prescribed 'Application for Non-Resident Tax Class Exemption' or 'Application for Exclusion from Withholding' before remittance. If treaty-reduced withholding was not applied at payment, the foreign shareholder may file a claim for refund with the National Tax Service within three years from the end of the calendar year in which the withholding occurred, but Korean tax authorities may broadly deny refunds when the recipient is considered a conduit or lacks substantive business activity.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Cross-border interest and royalty payments to non-resident lenders or licensors are subject to statutory withholding tax of 20% national tax plus 2% local surtax, aggregating 22%. Under the most common Korean income tax treaties, interest and royalty withholding rates are generally reduced to 10% to 15%, with interest on qualifying financial or commercial debt sometimes eligible for 10%, and royalties for patented or copyrighted digital technology often reduced to 10% to 15% depending on treaty-specific technical assistance clauses. The treaty-basis withholding is available only if the beneficial owner files the required Tax Residence Certificate and any statement of ownership or substance demanded by the Korean tax authority.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A Korean enterprise or foreign entity engaging in cross-border transactions with foreign related parties is required to prepare and file a Local File when the aggregate value of cross-border related-party transactions in the fiscal year exceeds KRW 5,000,000,000. The Master File is separately mandatory for a taxable year in which the annual consolidated revenue of the business group exceeds KRW 100,000,000,000. Foreign investors relying on transactional structure should also maintain benchmark studies and a contemporaneous economic substance file for any intragroup loan, algorithm licensing, or centralized fintech service supplied to the Korean platform.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea has not enacted OECD-style Economic Substance Regulations for domestic entities, but economic substance is enforced through the Korean CFC (Controlled Foreign Corporation) rules, the General Anti-Abuse Rule, and the tax treaty limitation-on-benefits application. A Chusik Hoesa used for P2P micro-lending must have actual management and control in Korea, a physical registered office with an operating function, local employees, board minutes prepared in Korea, and bank accounts through which the lending funds actually flow. The National Tax Service may recharacterize a Korean entity as a conduit if it finds the entity was inserted for treaty shopping, if the non-resident shareholder lacks genuine economic ownership of the income, or if the main beneficiaries of the lending algorithm or loan book are non-resident related parties without arm's-length remuneration.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting borrower interest income from the corporate income tax return, fabricating expenses for loan losses, inflating debt collection costs, creating shell SPVs to conceal fee income, or maintaining two sets of books for the P2P micro-lending platform.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: An unjustified understatement surcharge of 20% of the additional tax for negligence, escalated to 40% for fraud; criminal prosecution under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act with imprisonment for up to three years or fines of up to five times the evaded tax; daily late-payment interest of 0.022% on unpaid tax; and tax authorities may immediately collect additional taxes based on a corrected assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A director who knowingly signs a false tax return or authorizes concealing revenue may be jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate income tax to the extent of his or her fault; the National Tax Service may issue a personal collection order and asset freeze. Upon indictment, the director is subject to compulsory appearance in court, travel ban, surrender of passport, and imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Koreansource P2P lending interest and platform fees being de-minimis-misallocated to an offshore parent; allocation of excessive technology license fees or service fees to a related algorithm owner with zero economic function; loans from a foreign related party at below-market interest; unreported guarantee fees; or using an Irish/NV headquarters configuration without arm's-length compensation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Korean tax authority adjusts taxable income to the arm's-length result and imposes a 10% negligence surcharge on the additional assessed tax where transfer pricing documentation is not contemporaneous or is materially incomplete; where there is concealment, the surcharge increases to 20%; interest at the daily statutory rate accrues from the original due date. In serious cases, the taxpayer is removed from the mutual agreement procedure protection and exposed to adjusted withholding on constructive dividends.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorize avoided transfer-pricing adjustments while knowing underlying foreign related-party statements are false may be personally secondarily liable for unpaid corporation tax and the surcharges. Travel bans and forced-denaturalization disqualifications from future boards may be imposed where the non-compliance is systematic.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the Chusik Hoesa as an empty registration box: no physical office in Korea, no local employees, centralized board decisions in a tax haven, no underlying borrower underwriting or local risk management, or acting as a pure conduit for an offshore lending platform using Korea's treaty network only to relenter funds to Korean consumers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may apply the Korean GAAR to disregard the intermediary, re-source income to the beneficial owner, impose full 22% withholding on profits repatriated through the conduit, deny tax treaty relief, assess negligence surcharge of up to 40%, and reclassify loan repayments as deemed dividends. The entity itself can lose tax residency status if the place of effective management is found to be outside Korea, exposing the Korean entity to a deemed export and unlimited assessment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of a shell Chusik Hoesa who permit the entity to distribute phantom dividends or use corporate bank accounts for the principal lenders' liquidity may be personally liable under the Korean Commercial Act for unlawful distribution; criminal AML examinations may lead to travel bans under the Financial Information Act and imprisonment for money-laundering offenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the P2P micro-lending platform without a statutory online investment lending brokerage license or financial institution authorization; accepting client funds into the platform's own bank account without a separate Electronic Financial Transactions license; failure to file suspicious transaction reports for matched loan volume; or extending credit to politically exposed persons without enhanced due diligence.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Operation without a license under the Credit Business or Online Investment Lending rules exposes the Chusik Hoesa to administrative penalties, shutdown orders, fines up to KRW 200 million, and criminal prosecution punishable by up to five years' imprisonment. The statute of relative anti-money-laundering fines ranges from KRW 10 million to KRW 100 million per violation, and follow-up corrective orders may be published publicly.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers who knowingly allow unlicensed deposit-taking or fail to maintain AML transaction reporting are personally liable for unpaid regulatory fines; the prosecution routinely recommends travel bans, freezing of personal assets, and imprisonment for platform founders in the microlending fintech space. Directors cannot be indemnified by the corporate entity to cover AML penalties.
